patients.label: 26-year-old man with treatment-resistant paranoid schizophrenia treated with maintenance ECT

identity_evidence.quote: We present a case of a 26-year-old male patient with a TRS.

attribution_limitations: The abstract describes a treatment series of ECT sessions plus a course of 24 M-ECTs, while the case text says 24 ECT treatments were administered in total over 1 year and evaluates after 24 ECT sessions; the source does not say whether the acute series is part of the 24. No second number is printed for one value, so this is an ambiguity, not a source conflict.

All numeric PSYRATS and PANSS item and subscale scores are printed only inside the Table 1 and Table 2 images (pixel content in visual.json); the text states only qualitative changes, so no numeric observation facts are recorded.

The abstract and discussion say PSYRATS scores for negative symptoms decreased, and the discussion names blunted affect and emotional withdrawal, while the Table 1 image lists only auditory hallucination and delusion subscales; PANSS in Table 2 is the table that lists negative symptoms.

The case text says no add-on psychiatric in-house treatment was needed during the whole M-ECT course, while the discussion mentions frequent welfare during his stays at the hospital as a possible confounder; the setting of ECT delivery and the hospital stays are not described.

The text says the patient was followed up for approximately 3 years for schizophrenia, with symptoms since age 20 and a current age of 26; the source does not state when the diagnosis was made or how the 3 years relate to the 6 years since onset.

The text says a stay at a forensic psychiatry clinic and aggressive tendencies "could be prevented due to the treatment"; no forensic stay or aggression is described in the case presentation and the causal claim is the authors.

The abstract says the entire treatment was tolerated without significant side effects and the discussion says no side effects were reported and another sentence reports good tolerance and compliance; the exact scope (ECT series versus M-ECT) is not stated for each sentence.

The patient had memory deficits as a disease symptom before ECT and the discussion says he reported no side effects such as memory impairment; these are different time contexts and no post-ECT memory assessment is described.

In the Table 1 (PSYRATS) image the auditory-hallucination after-treatment item scores do not add up to the printed after-treatment subscale score (one point apart), and the printed subscale maximum does not equal the item count times the Likert maximum. Table values are pixel content kept only in visual.json.
